History:
- Chief complaint: Pain/stinging with urination (dysuria) for a few days.
- Onset/duration/progression: Began a few days ago; bothersome but not severe; unchanged despite OTC bicarbonate.
- Context/associated symptoms:
  - Lower abdominal (suprapubic) crampy discomfort with urination; non-radiating; distinct from menstrual cramps.
  - Small amount of visible blood in urine earlier today.
  - Urine has an unusual odor.
  - Denies fever, nausea, vomiting, flank pain, back pain.
  - Denies increased urinary frequency; urgency not discussed.
  - Denies vaginal discharge.
- Gynecologic/sexual history:
  - Sexually active with a boyfriend of a couple of months; uses condoms.
  - LMP: “a couple of weeks ago.” Doctor restated as “three weeks ago” (conflict noted).
  - Thinks pregnancy is unlikely; has never had an STI screen.
- Prior episodes: Not reported.

Past Medical History:
- IBS.
- Allergies: Clindamycin → swelling.
- Medications: No regular medications.
  - Tried OTC bicarbonate recently for symptoms; not helpful.
- Family history: Denies kidney/bladder/bowel disease.
- Social: 19-year-old college student (biology); lives with roommates; non-smoker; drinks alcohol socially on weekends.

Physical Examination:
- Not recorded.
- Relevant negatives by history: No fever; no flank/back pain; no nausea/vomiting; alert and conversational on call.

Impression:
- Acute uncomplicated cystitis (lower UTI) in a healthy young woman, given short-duration dysuria, suprapubic discomfort, malodorous urine, and brief gross hematuria, without systemic features.
- DDx (consistent with transcript):
  - Urethritis due to STI (chlamydia/gonorrhea/mycoplasma): Dysuria with new partner and no prior STI screen; may occur without discharge.
  - Vaginitis (BV/trichomonas) causing external dysuria: Malodor noted, though absence of discharge/pruritus lowers likelihood.

Management Plan:
- Antibiotics: Nitrofurantoin or trimethoprim prescribed, 1 tablet twice daily for 3 days (dose/strength not documented).
- Hydration: Increase fluid intake to help flush the urinary tract.
- Symptomatic options: Cranberry juice may help.
- Sexual activity: Avoid intercourse until symptoms resolve; continue barrier contraception thereafter.
- Return precautions: Call/return if not improved by end of the week or sooner for fever, back/flank pain, or if feeling more unwell (concern for ascending infection).
- Pregnancy: Advised to obtain a pregnancy test to rule out pregnancy if there is any concern.
- Follow-up: Contact clinician if symptoms persist or worsen.

Patient Summary:
- 19-year-old woman with a few days of stinging on urination, mild suprapubic cramps with voiding, malodorous urine, and a brief episode of visible hematuria; no fever or flank pain.
- Clinical picture most consistent with acute uncomplicated cystitis.
- Started short-course antibiotics and advised hydration, temporary abstinence, and return precautions.

Key Takeaways:
- Take prescribed antibiotic as directed: 1 tablet twice daily for 3 days.
- Drink plenty of fluids; you may try cranberry juice.
- Seek care urgently if fever, back/flank pain, or worsening symptoms develop.

Next Steps:
- If symptoms are not improving after antibiotics or recur, consider urinalysis/urine culture and STI testing (NAAT for chlamydia/gonorrhea), given sexual activity and no prior screen.
- Perform pregnancy test if any concern for pregnancy.
- Follow up with the clinician by end of week if not better.

Quality checks:
● Missing expected elements: No vitals; no physical exam; no urinalysis or urine culture; exact antibiotic choice and dose/strength not documented; pregnancy test not performed; no STI testing performed; pain severity not quantified.  
● Conflicts between transcript and DDx: LMP documented by patient as “a couple of weeks ago,” restated by doctor as “three weeks ago” (conflict noted).  
● Transcript quality: Minor audio issues/overlap in a few responses (e.g., initial connectivity; fever question), but core history understandable.
